best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional ATK% boost and an additional 5% ATK% for every 1.5 seconds the equipped character has been actively on-field - up to 20% after 6 seconds, totalling 30% additional ATK% after fully ramped. This set is completely incompatible with quickswap playstyles, but for the hypercarry playstyle Lingyang will generally use, this is his best set by a small margin.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Very easy echo to use that should be used at the very beginning of the burst window right after the Intro. Thanks to its instant cast there is no thinking required and you can enjoy your ATK% boost and some nice burst damage.

best_echo_sets.commentary: This set grants permanent Resonance Skill DMG% and even bigger Glacio and Skill DMG increases when casting Skill and Liberation respectively. While the second Skill DMG boost is not upkept consistently by Lingyang, he does benefit from the stat and the Glacio DMG boost is additionally appreciated, making it his second best set and his best set that can be used in quickswap compositions.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: The Sentry Construct is the most effective Main echo choice for Frosty Resolve users thanks to its passive 12% Glacio and Resonance Skill DMG% bonuses which are active at all times. The transformation ability of Sentry Construct is also powerful, swap cancellable, usable in the air and accessible more often than other Echoes, thanks to its ability to recharge cooldown when the user activates their Resonance Liberation.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Glacio DMG% boost and up to an additional 30% Glacio DMG% after you land 3 Basic or Heavy Attacks for a grand total of 40% additional Glacio damage after fully ramped.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Provides a total of 12% Glacio and Skill DMG boosts when casting all 3 hits for 15s, deals a good amount of damage and freezes enemies for a short duration on the final hit. All great things, but the problem with this Echo is that it takes a while to cast and is best used pre-rotation before Intro by swap cancelling out of the final hit. This takes a lot of time to execute and is the main reason why Freezing Frost does not rank above other Glacio damage-focused sets like Frosty Resolve.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Iuno's Signature is Lingyang's best choice by virtue of its really high CRIT Rate boost, its good ATK stats, and its 36% Liberation DMG DEF Ignore and 20% DMG Bonus effects which can fully apply to Lingyang's initial Ultimate cast. In other words, the CRIT and ATK stats are great for Lingyang and it makes his initial Ultimate cast damage go way up, which makes it the best choice.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Zani's Signature offers high ATK, CRIT DMG and 8% DEF Ignore for 6s when casting Basic Attacks, which is easily upkept throughout most of Lingyang's rotation. Overall a very strong generalist Gauntlets choice.

best_weapons.commentary_details: High Base ATK, a good CRIT Rate stat, 12% Attribute DMG Bonus unconditionally and 48% Liberation DMG Bonus when casting Ultimate as well. Xiangli Yao's weapon provides lots of good stats, making it a highly competitive weapon choice for Lingyang.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Increases ATK by a good amount but also has a very niche Flat Energy restoration effect when casting Skill which helps alleviate Lingyang's Energy Regen requirements, which makes it a strong 4-star alternative.

cons: Damage ceiling is just on the cusp of being at the same level as the other viable F2P DPS characters (e.g Encore), but he barely doesn't get there so he's generally not worth it for anything beyond Matrix high scores;
Difficult to utilize in Quickswap and even more difficult to justify there;
Low initial Concerto Energy generation can make Opener rotations inconsistent;
Tune Break Skills put him on the ground when he wants to be in the air for basically all of his rotation - the same can happen if he gets interrupted mid-air;
Fear him, for he is Lingyang, destroyer of 50/50s.
pros: Super easy to pick up and pretty easy to optimize;
Pretty decent enemy tracking with his optimized rotation, and can hit airborne enemies thanks to his affinity for mid-air combat;
Low reliance on limited weapons as a permanent banner character, and has access to decent F2P teammates.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Lingyang is a 5-star Glacio Gauntlets DPS who focuses on mid-air combat in his 10s-long Forte stance that he needs to make the most of in order to deal damage. His goal will be to quickly rack up Forte and then leap into the air to use a mix of Basic Attacks and Skills in order to deal the most damage possible within his Forte stance duration.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Building up Lingyang's initial Forte bar to full, which he can easily do with a combination of his Intro and Ultimate, enables him to cast a special Heavy Attack called Glorious Plunge. This sends him into the Striding Lion state for up to 10s, during which he gains access to much stronger Basic Attacks and Skills than unusual (though in his case, it's more like they start dealing decent levels of damage).

His Ultimate also gives him access to a 50% Glacio DMG Bonus self-buff for 14s, and his Outro simply deals a good chunk of extra damage to enemies. Lastly, once his Forte has been almost completely expended, he can finish his rotation with the lengthy Stormy Kicks Basic Attack, which deals a decent amount of damage and restores a lot of Concerto. Ideally, Lingyang should Swap Cancel this attack on the first rotation if he generates the required Concerto for it. This is difficult to do, but it can really save a lot of time on his future rotations thanks to how much Concerto he carries over into the next rotation this way.

Finally, let's talk about his rotations. As explained earlier, Lingyang wants to immediately cast his Ultimate to benefit from his 50% Glacio DMG Bonus self-buff. After an Intro, this gives him enough Forte to cast Glorious Plunge. However, you have 2 options for his rotation inside of Striding Lion state. He can either do a mix of Basic Attacks and Skills, as casting a Skill in between his Basic Attacks doesn't interrupt the chain. Repeating this 5 times total is his normal dev-intended rotation, but he can also choose to really lean into his Skill damage.

One of his passives, called Diligent Practice, balances his otherwise weak Skill damage into being his strongest attack by a decent margin. It essentially adds an extra hit of damage equivalent to 150% of his usual Skill DMG if he has cast a Basic Attack beforehand, which makes his Diligent Practice 2.5x stronger than it otherwise would be. While this is useless to know with his S6 involved or a Basic Attack DMG buffer, as in both of these cases his Basic Attack DMG should be utilized, it's actually possible to trigger the Diligent Practice effect without even casting any Basic Attacks whatsoever.

Indeed, if any of Lingyang's Skill animations are completed and he starts walking in Striding Lion state, after a Skill has been cast and the Basic Attack button is still being held down, the DIligent Practice effect will trigger over and over even if you keep chaining Skills without any Basic Attacks involved. While this is definitely not dev-intended, it brings his damage up by a slight amount, particularly being useful with Skill DMG buffers like Zhezhi in the mix, or simply alongside general buffers like Lynae. This is his most optimized rotation without a Basic Attack DMG buffer or his S6 involved.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Even when considering the new developments to Lingyang's rotation, it's safe to say his base damage numbers do not allow him to compete anywhere near the level of modern damage dealers. While this is expected of a permanent banner DPS, his level, even when optimized, is far below that of any modern or better F2P damage dealer. Electro Rover and Encore are both options that undeniably outclass Lingyang, making him quite niche and in most cases, a completely skippable investment.

Unless your Lingyang has very high Sequences available to him, he'll never get close to the level of any DPS like even Carlotta. The release of his new best teammates Lynae and Mornye, a slightly better weapon in the form of Iuno's Signature, and a plethora of new Glacio DMG-oriented Echo sets have not really helped his situation. In general, from a meta perspective, he remains a questionable investment unless you're trying to seriously optimize your Matrix score with every damage dealer that you have available.

In conclusion, Lingyang is not going to be a worthwhile investment for the majority of players in Wuthering Waves. Until he gets significant buffs to his damage ceiling, he will not be able to compete by modern endgame content standards, and while he has access to good F2P teammates like Sanhua and Verina, they're usually better used elsewhere, typically on limited characters or better F2P damage dealers like Encore or even Electro Rover.

synergies.commentary: Lingyang's best partners. Lynae has the strongest generalist buffs in the game and makes for a particularly strong core with Mornye to deal extra Tune Break damage and provide some the strongest array of buffs Lingyang can have. Zhezhi is also very strong by virtue of sporting good personal damage off-field via Coordinated Attacks and amazing 20% Glacio and 25% Skill DMG buffs on Outro that Lingyang very much appreciates.

One of the fastest rotation times in the game with a very good 38% Basic ATK DMG Amplify buff on Outro allows her to buff Lingyang a great amount, and allows him to take the spotlight by doing most of the team's damage. Often used if Zhezhi is taken up by another team or if you don't own her since Sanhua's free.

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
